title: Drona: Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Drona's death
hook: a young warrior knows how to break into the wheel formation, and says out loud that he doesn't know the way out
carry: one man at the gap undid it

segments.voice: Yesterday Drona took command and promised to capture Yudhishthira, if only Arjuna were away. Your line: the empty space where Arjuna should be. Today, Arjuna is away.

Morning, and across the field Drona has arranged his army into a shape the Pandavas dread: the chakra, the wheel. Ring inside ring of chariots, elephants and warriors, turning to close around anyone who comes near. On the Pandava side, only a few know how to break it. Arjuna knows. Krishna knows. And Arjuna is far away on the other side of the field, answering the sworn ones' challenge, just as the plan intended. Yudhishthira looks around and finds one more person who might know: Arjuna's son, Abhimanyu.
screen: `THE WHEEL FORMATION.` → `ARJUNA IS FAR AWAY.` → `ARJUNA'S SON, ABHIMANYU.`

segments.voice: Abhimanyu is the son of Arjuna and Subhadra, Krishna's sister: young, fearless and already a fine warrior. Yudhishthira asks him to break the wheel. His answer is honest in a way that's hard to read. In Ganguli's telling, he says he knows how to pierce the formation, but if trouble comes, he won't be able to come out again. Some retellings add a story that he learned the way in while still in his mother's womb, hearing it explained, and that she fell asleep before the way out. The epic passage here simply has him say what he knows and what he doesn't. Yudhishthira and Bhima reassure him. You break in, they say, and we'll follow right behind you, through the gap you make. So Abhimanyu drives in. He breaks the ring, and he's inside, fighting brilliantly. But behind him the gap doesn't stay open. Jayadratha, the king of Sindhu, rides into the breach. The text says he once won a gift from Shiva: for one day he could hold back all the Pandavas except Arjuna. This is that day. Bhima, Yudhishthira and the others hurl themselves at the opening and can't get through. The wheel closes. One young man is inside, alone, surrounded by Drona's army. The plan was sound, the courage was real, and one man at the gap undid it.
screen: `ARJUNA'S SON` · `"I KNOW THE WAY IN, NOT OUT"` · `"WE'LL FOLLOW YOU"` · then, large: `JAYADRATHA HOLDS THE GAP`

segments.voice: Think of something you're good at starting but not finishing: a project, a conversation, a habit. Breathe in and name the part you know; breathe out and name, honestly, the part you don't know yet, the way Abhimanyu said both. If you pray, that unknown part can go into your prayer.
Drona. Today his wheel formation closes around Arjuna's son, with the gap held shut behind him.
Your line: one man at the gap undid it. The way in was known; the way out was not. Day eight hundred thirty-two, done.

trapdoor: what you thought: Abhimanyu didn't know enough.
what it means: he told them exactly what he didn't know, and they promised to cover it.
what a scholar hears: the trap isn't only the formation; it's the gap Jayadratha holds, by a boon that works for one day.

chat.says: Why did Abhimanyu get trapped inside the wheel formation?
options: Jayadratha held the gap shut behind him, so the others couldn't follow in.
He rode in alone because he refused to wait for Bhima's help.
Arjuna had told him to stay inside and hold the center until dark.
chat.meaning: Abhimanyu broke in, trusting the others to follow. Jayadratha, with Shiva's one-day gift, held the gap, and the wheel closed behind him.

Abhimanyu.meaning: the young son of Arjuna and Subhadra

Jayadratha.meaning: the king of Sindhu, who holds the gap shut

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli Abhimanyu's words that he can pierce the array but cannot come out if danger arises, and Yudhishthira and Bhima's promise to follow.
